To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) an autonomous intrinsic motivation system can drive a robot to explore and learn in an unsupervised manner, (2) such a system can be implemented in a modular way by combining a measure of the progress of learning and an exploration function, (3) the system can be used to build a developmental sequence of activities, and (4) the system is robust enough to be used in a physical robot, and can be applied to real-world problems.

the mechanism of Intelligent adaptive curiosity, a drive towards situations of intermediate difficulty, is able to autonomously organize a robot's activities in a stage-like manner and to make it learn to manipulate objects in a way similar to a child's behavior.
the robot is driven by an intrinsic motivation system, that it autonomously develops complex behaviors, and that the complexity of its activities increases over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how a robot can autonomously organize its activities in order to develop its own mental capabilities.
the question of how to design a robot with the capacity for self-organized mental development.
the question of whether it is possible to endow machines with an intrinsic motivation system that pushes them to autonomously develop their own mental structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper has made a significant contribution to the field.
the mechanism of intelligent adaptive curiosity is able to generate an autonomous developmental sequence of activities in the robot.
the mechanism of Intelligent adaptive curiosity is able to generate developmental sequences of increasing complexity in an autonomous manner, without being explicitly programmed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robot's behavior is organized in a manner that can be considered as developmental.

a robot endowed with an intrinsic motivation system can exhibit developmental sequences of increasing complexity, which are not preprogrammed, but emerge from the robot's own interactions with the environment.
we have shown that the robot can autonomously develop an intrinsic motivation system for exploration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robot's drive to learn is not a simple drive to explore.
the mechanism of Intelligent adaptive Curiosity can be used to endow robots with intrinsic motivation systems, which permit the autonomous organization of their behavior.
the intrinsic motivation of the agent is the key to the emergence of developmental sequences, which are not pre-programmed but emerge from the interaction between the agent and its environment.
